newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE SEES HIGH GROWTH, LOW INFLATION, MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: GREECE SEES HIGH GROWTH, LOW INFLATION, MINISTER.

text.p: Greece expects GDP growth of 3.3 percent in 1997, well above the EU average and compared to 2.6 percent in 1996, National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou told reporters.
He forecast an average inflation rate of 6.5 percent in 1997, down from 8.5 percent in 1996, and set a year-end 1997 inflation target of 4.5 percent.
Papandoniou was speaking after a full cabinet meeting on the 1997 budget which must be presented to parliament by the end of this month.
He predicted Greece's 1997 budget deficit would fall to 4.2 percent of GDP, compared to 7.6 percent in 1996.

Earlier, Prime Minister Costas Simitis said Greece must meet its EU economic convergence targets. He said he was planning spending cuts, the first taxation of interest on T-bills and bonds, and abolishing an array of tax exemptions. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
